layers.name: Deep Background
layers.paintingTip: Start with a wash of Payne's Gray or Indigo for a deep, dark base on a large brush (e.g., flat 1-inch).

layers.name: Background Glow
layers.description: A subtle, dark yellowish-brown glow at the bottom of the background.
layers.paintingTip: Using a soft, damp mop brush (size 12), apply a very diluted wash of Burnt Umber and a touch of Cadmium Yellow Deep, allowing it to softly bleed into the dark background.

layers.name: Back Leaf/Stem
layers.description: A dark, blurry leaf or stem element in the mid-ground, behind the flower.
layers.paintingTip: With a large, soft round brush (size 10), apply a very diluted mix of Dioxazine Purple and Sepia, keeping the edges soft and indistinct to create a blurred effect.

layers.name: Flower Base Petals
layers.description: The underlying, darker parts of the flower petals, forming the cup shape.
layers.paintingTip: Using a medium round brush (size 8), lay down a base wash of Quinacridone Magenta mixed with a touch of Ultramarine Violet, focusing on the deeper shadowed areas of the petals.

layers.name: Flower Main Petals
layers.description: The vibrant, translucent main body of the flower petals.
layers.paintingTip: With a medium round brush (size 6), apply a vibrant wash of Opera Pink or Permanent Rose, allowing the color to be slightly lighter and more translucent at the edges. Use lifting techniques with a damp brush for subtle highlights.

layers.name: Stamen Filaments
layers.description: The thin, purple stalks of the stamens.
layers.paintingTip: Using a fine liner brush (size 00), carefully paint thin lines with a concentrated mix of Dioxazine Purple and a touch of Payne's Gray for depth.

layers.name: Stamen Anthers
layers.description: The bright yellow pollen-bearing tips of the stamens.
layers.paintingTip: With a small, pointed round brush (size 2), dab concentrated Cadmium Yellow Light or Indian Yellow for the anthers, ensuring they stand out brightly.

layers.name: Stamen Hairs & Pistil
layers.description: Fine white hairs on the filaments and the white stigma of the pistil.
layers.paintingTip: Using a very fine rigger brush (size 000) and opaque white gouache or a very thick mix of Titanium White watercolor, carefully paint the delicate hairs and the small stigma. Ensure minimal water to maintain opacity.

layers.name: Foreground Leaf/Stem
layers.description: The dark, slightly more defined leaf or stem supporting the flower in the foreground.
layers.paintingTip: Using a medium flat brush (size 6), apply a concentrated mix of Perylene Violet and Sepia for the dark leaf, allowing some texture to show. Use dry brush technique for subtle highlights on the edge.
